interest: Index of intelligence on Japan's military and war economy.
overview: This file comprises State Department docket sheets (Lists of Papers) filed under decimal classification 894.20 (Military Affairs: Japan) spanning 1940 through 1944. The recorded entries index incoming and outgoing telegrams, despatches, military attaché reports, intelligence memoranda, and cross-reference notices detailing Japanese military policy, defense legislation, force deployments, and war mobilization. Major subjects covered include the Japanese Army and Navy's political influence in the cabinet, the enactment and imperial enforcement ordinances of the National Defense Security Law and National General Mobilization Law, military movements and command reorganizations in French Indochina and China, coastal and anti-aircraft defenses in Osaka and Tokyo, and intelligence assessments of Japanese industrial war potential under Allied blockade. The sheets also catalogue reports on regional defenses in Hokkaido, contraband fortified zone charts, overseas technical assistance, and diplomatic agreements including the 1944 transfer of Japanese oil and coal concessions in Northern Sakhalin to the Soviet Union.

subfiles.about: A six-page cumulative State Department docket list registering official communications and intelligence reports concerning Japanese military affairs, defense laws, and war mobilization from late 1940 to April 1944.
subfiles.summary: This six-page register (Sheets 23 through 28) indexes documents 894.20/245 through 894.20/311 relating to Japanese military developments before and during World War II. Early entries document the growing political assertiveness of the military in the cabinet, legislative enactments including the National Defense Security Law and National General Mobilization Law, and Japanese troop concentrations and command shifts in Indochina and China. Later entries record defense precautions such as Osaka road work and Tokyo anti-aircraft batteries, British economic intelligence investigations into Japanese blockade endurance, and reports from private citizens and former consular officials regarding fortifications in Hokkaido. The final entries note wartime industrial conversions to aircraft engine production and Ambassador Harriman's report on the 1944 Soviet-Japanese protocol transferring North Sakhalin concessions.
